newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX says holders support Bell merger.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX says holders support Bell merger.

text.p: NYNEX Corp said on Wednesday that based on a preliminary count, shareholders support the company's merger with Bell Atlantic Corp.

"In plain Engish: It is a go," said Frederic Salerno, NYNEX chief financial officer. He said the company has three quarters of shareholders' votes returned and about 96 percent are in support of the merger.
The company stressed that the count is not final.
NYNEX expects the merger to close in early 1997.

Ivan Seidenberg, NYNEX's chairman and chief executive, said at a press conference before a shareholders' meeting held for a vote on the merger that he expected the Department of Justice to approve the merger by the middle of December. About 30 days to 45 days after that decision, the company should close the deal, he said.

Also, the company said it and Bell Atlantic reached an agreement last night with the Communications Workers of America union that outlines a framework for the relationship between the CWA and the newly-merged entity, Bell Atlantic.

"We are confident there is a mutual trust between the companies and the CWA that will enable the merged company and the members of the CWA to grow and succeed together," said Morton Bahr, CWA's president, in a written statement.

The agreement, a loosely worded compact that pledges mutual trust and commitment, ensures the union its exisitng labor contract will be honored through its August 1998 expiration date. The company said it reaffirmed its commitment to the labor contract, promising to make no further layoffs or forced transfers and to not transfer major groups of employees between Bell Atlantic and NYNEX.
NYNEX said the companies are still in talks with the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers union regarding the IBEW's support of the merger.
The company said it had a total of 90,000 CWA and IBEW employees at both companies.
NYNEX and Bell Atlantic announced their merger proposal, valued at about $22 billion, in April. Bell Atlantic shareholders are scheduled to vote Nov. 8 on the deal.
